original_title: Interfacial Water‐Networks Regulate the Anodic Stability of Carbon Electrodes
title: Interfacial water's hydrogen-bond network decides how fast your carbon electrode dies
blurb: Operando DEMS and in situ ATR spectroscopy trace carbon electrode oxidation at positive potentials back to the hydrogen-bonding network of interfacial water, not just the carbon's own structure. Most fixes so far have targeted the carbon itself, so reframing the water at the interface as the thing to control is the actual news here.

original_title: Promoting Efficient H2 Dissociation in Photothermal CO2 Hydrogenation through Functional Separation and Synergistic Coupling of Active Sites
title: Splitting up the jobs in a photothermal CO2-to-fuel catalyst
blurb: A Cu-In bimetallic catalyst on CeO2 spatially separates plasmonic light harvesting, H2 activation, and CO2 conversion onto different sites instead of making one site do everything. That separation is what boosts H2 dissociation and spillover, backed by transient and operando spectroscopy rather than just a performance number.

original_title: A Readily Scalable Silylated Cyclic Allyl Sulfide Monomer for Degradable Vinyl Polymers
title: A cyclic sulfide monomer that finally makes vinyl polymers degradable without giving up radical polymerization
blurb: Radical ring-opening copolymerization is the standard trick for slipping degradable linkages into vinyl polymers, but every cyclic monomer so far has traded off efficiency, versatility, or scalability. This silylated cyclic allyl sulfide claims all three at once, including a synthesis route the authors say scales. Worth watching whether "readily scalable" survives contact with an actual plant.

original_title: CD44 Receptor-Guided Hyaluronic Acid Nanogels with Dual-Stimuli Responsiveness and Lysosomal Disruption Capability for In Vivo Protein Delivery in Lung Cancer Treatment.
title: Hyaluronic acid nanogels that target CD44 and break out of the lysosome to deliver protein into lung tumors
blurb: Hyaluronic acid nanogels built to home in on CD44-overexpressing cells, respond to two separate triggers, and rupture the lysosome once inside so the payload protein actually reaches the cytoplasm instead of getting degraded. Tested in vivo in lung cancer models. No potency numbers here, just the design.

original_title: Dual-Crosslinked Sesbania Gum-Derived Antibacterial Hydrogel Enriched with Multiple Active Sites for Efficient Skin Tissue Engineering.
title: A gum-derived hydrogel for wound dressing, cross-linked twice and antibacterial by design
blurb: Sesbania gum hydrogel with a dual crosslinked network and multiple active sites baked in, pitched for skin tissue engineering where you want both mechanical hold and antibacterial action in one dressing.

original_title: DOTMP induces nephrotoxicity via the Hsp90β/PI3K signaling axis.
title: DOTMP's kidney toxicity traced to the Hsp90β/PI3K pathway
blurb: DOTMP, the bone-targeting chelator used in radiopharmaceutical formulations, causes nephrotoxicity, and the authors pin the mechanism on Hsp90β/PI3K signaling. Worth knowing if you're the one dosing it, mechanism aside.

original_title: Biphasic Polyarylisocyanide Liquid Crystals with Enhanced Enantiodiscrimination for Residual Chemical Shift Anisotropy Measurements
title: A liquid crystal that splits in two, so you get RCSAs instead of just RDCs
blurb: Residual dipolar couplings get all the attention in anisotropic NMR, while residual chemical shift anisotropies have been stuck behind clunky acquisition methods. This biphasic lyotropic liquid crystal, built from single-handed helical polyisocyanides via alkyne-Pd(II) polymerization, uses its own two-phase nature plus enhanced chiral discrimination to make RCSA measurements easy to get. A methods paper, but one that opens up a measurement people have mostly skipped.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Amino Acid, Peptide, and Protein Level Mapping of Lysozyme Oxidation by Ozone-Dominated Nonthermal Plasma.
title: Mapping exactly where ozone plasma oxidizes lysozyme, residue by residue
blurb: Nonthermal plasma dominated by ozone chews on lysozyme, and this maps the damage at the amino acid, peptide, and whole-protein level instead of just reporting bulk oxidation. Useful if you're using plasma to sanitize food proteins and want to know what you're actually doing to them.

original_title: Low-Temperature Aqueous Upgrading of Waste PET Plastics into Metal–Organic Frameworks with Confined PdNi Clusters for High-Performance Semihydrogenation of Alkynes
title: Turning waste PET bottles into the MOF that hosts your alkyne hydrogenation catalyst
blurb: Alkyne semihydrogenation always fights the same tradeoff, push selectivity and you lose activity or vice versa. Here the MOF host confining PdNi clusters is made straight from waste PET plastic via a low-temperature aqueous route, so the sustainability claim covers the support too, not just the metal loading. Turning bottles into catalyst scaffolding is a neat trick regardless of how the hydrogenation numbers stack up against other confined-cluster catalysts.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

original_title: Photochemical Cobalt-Catalyzed Formal Hydroacylation via Radical 1,2-Carbonyl Migration
title: Cobalt MHAT shuffles a carbonyl one carbon over to fake a hydroacylation
blurb: Radical 1,2-carbonyl migration usually needs some pre-installed handle or is boxed in by whatever radical kicks off the reaction. Here a photocatalytic cobalt MHAT step does it under mild reductive conditions straight from β,γ-unsaturated ketones, migrating the carbonyl to give a formally hydroacylated product without running an actual hydroacylation. A rearrangement dressed up as a different reaction, which is sort of the fun of it.

original_title: Hydrogels at the Biology-Physics-Chemistry Interface: Design Principles Guiding Emerging Frontiers.
title: A field guide to designing hydrogels where biology, physics, and chemistry actually have to agree
blurb: A perspective piece laying out design principles for hydrogels that sit at the overlap of biology, physics, and chemistry, the kind of roundup meant to orient people before they start mixing fields. Light on new data, heavy on framework.

original_title: DHTA-modified CuCe layered double hydroxide-reinforced Gelatin/oxidized starch hydrogel pads: Synergistic antibiosis, antioxidation, and Ammonia sensing for shrimp fresh-keeping.
title: A hydrogel pad that kills bacteria, mops up oxidants, and tells you when your shrimp are going bad
blurb: DHTA-modified CuCe layered double hydroxide reinforces a gelatin/oxidized starch hydrogel pad doing three jobs at once on packed shrimp: antibacterial, antioxidant, and ammonia sensing to flag spoilage before you smell it. A food-packaging paper chasing the full multitasking checklist in one pad.

original_title: Disorder Beats Order: Carbon Microstructure Steers Radical Versus Cationic Pathways in Kolbe Electrolysis
title: The messier the carbon electrode, the more selective the chemistry
blurb: Kolbe electrolysis is the classic radical C–C coupling used across fuel and pharma synthesis, and it turns out the carbon electrode's microstructure, not just its surface chemistry, decides whether you get the radical pathway or a cationic side reaction. They ran eight electrodes across two sets, commercial carbons with different macro-architectures and carbon nanofibers with tuned graphitization, and the disordered carbons were the ones steering selectivity toward the radical route. Counterintuitive if you assumed a cleaner, more ordered electrode would give cleaner chemistry.

original_title: Stress-Induced Covalent Labelling and Tandem Fluorogenicity for Tri-State Warning of Fluohepatotoxicity-Associated Mitochondrial Damage
title: A probe that only lights up once mitochondria are actually stressed
blurb: Most mitochondrial damage dyes just accumulate electrostatically or get pre-labelled in, which makes them bad at telling you anything about an ongoing or specific stress event. This one instead covalently labels only after a particular stressor hits, then reports through a tandem fluorogenic readout with three distinct states, aimed at flagging the mitochondrial damage tied to liver toxicity. More of a diagnostic tool upgrade than a discovery, but a real fix for a genuine blind spot in how that damage gets monitored.

original_title: Intramolecular Michael Addition Explain the Diastereoselectivity in the Total Synthesis of (±)-Stemocurtisine by Prof. Mingji Dai
title: Intramolecular Michael Addition Explain the Diastereoselectivity in the Total Synthesis of (±)-Stemocurtisine by Prof. Mingji Dai
blurb: https://preview.redd.it/92xu4sxm47xh1.png?width=595&format=png&auto=webp&s=e72917879b6cfaa02163a6e2082f2a0ded72092d In the total synthesis of (±)-stemocurtisine, a MOM-protected enone undergoes Et₂Zn/O₂ epoxidation with dr >20:1. Could the MOM ether oxygen undergo intramolecular Michael addition to the enone, forming a five-membered cyclic oxonium intermediate that directs the subsequent epoxidation? Is this mechanism chemically plausible? I'd appreciate your thoughts!
